pensamiento:
I'm checking the user story against the quality criteria one by one. The role and action are present, so QUS-001 passes, even though "Mike" reads more like a name than a role. It has a single objective, has no extra detail, and its benefit is about understanding how much the product is used, so QUS-002 through QUS-004 pass too.

I'm going through the rest of the criteria: the story is atomic, minimal, and conceptually sound, and it's still uniform with the English backlog items, so those pass. Where it falls short is the lack of a measure for "some metrics" and "how much," so QUS-006 fails. It also has no defined metrics, time window, or acceptance criteria, so INV-003 and INV-005 fail, while the independence, value, and size checks look fine.

I'm going through the remaining criteria: the DOR checks don't really apply here, since there are no external dependencies, no clear business-rule limits, and no high-volume or critical NFR, though the missing metric definitions get folded into the INV-003 finding. That leaves three defects to flag, QUS-006 and INV-003 as major and INV-005 as blocking, so my decision is to send it back.

I'm settling on the estimate of 1, since the story doesn't define a scope I can size, and the rule for that case gives exactly that value. I'm also going to skip the reference-scale lookup, because 1 already sits on the scale. Next I'm looking at a refined version of the story, keeping its role, action, and benefit as they are while noting the gaps the criteria flagged.

I'm drafting a refined version of the story now, keeping the role and benefit as they are. I'm also weighing whether "Mike" should be flagged as a name rather than a role, and I'm going to frame the recommendations as questions instead of adding requirements.

I'm settling on the defect list for this one: QUS-006 and INV-003 as major, and INV-005 as blocking. Since nothing here defines a scope I can size, I'm treating the return as the outcome, and I'll leave the acceptance criteria empty.

Aportar el alcance necesario para estimar: qué métricas se muestran, periodo de agregación, fuente de los datos (cómo se registra el uso del juego), quién puede consultarlas y en qué formato. Sin esto el equipo tendría que preguntar antes de estimar.

Agregar criterios de aceptación como reglas u observables, por ejemplo: 'Dado un periodo seleccionado, cuando Mike consulta las métricas, entonces se muestran [MÉTRICA] calculada sobre [PERIODO]'. Deben poder comprobarse sin interpretación.
